cross_response_observations: The dominant failure category across responses A through G is some structural break in the upstream specification of either the move set, the base case, the P/N convention, or the dynamic-programming recurrence. Responses B, F, and G all involve a wrong move set (B drops 1, F includes 0, G enumerates a non-Fibonacci sequence) but each via a different mechanism, so all three appear together only in the broad 'wrong-move-set' category and disagree on which specific code applies. Responses A, B, and G all assert a false periodicity for the P-positions (typical claims: period 4, period 7, period 11), and all three exhibit arithmetic recursion errors when the assumed period is forced onto positions where the Fibonacci recurrence actually produces an irregular 4-6 spacing. Responses D, E, and G truncate the output string before 101 characters; for D the truncation co-occurs with a flipped base case, for E with a Sprague-Grundy misapplication, and for G with the wrong Fibonacci enumeration. Response C is the structurally cleanest deviation: a consistent P/N convention swap that inverts every label without otherwise breaking the DP, producing a string that is essentially the bitwise complement of the gold. Response H is pathological: it loops or truncates before committing to a final classification, so non_terminating_or_no_final_answer is its only applicable code. The single most common downstream code is arithmetic_recursion_error, present in six of the eight responses; it almost never appears as the load-bearing primary diagnostic because in each case some upstream error (move set, base case, convention, or framework) accounts for the wrong labels.
